# RiskScope synthetic data pack

**All data here is SYNTHETIC.** It is generated by `generate_synthetic.py` (seed 42) from a factor model with fat-tailed noise and stylised market regimes. It exists so you can see what every stage of the ML pipeline looks like and develop against realistic shapes. It is not real market history. Do not put its numbers on a slide. The final `eval.json` for the pitch must come from Hardik's real yfinance cache.

## Files

| File | What it is | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| `universe.csv` | The 36 assets: ticker, name, sector, market, currency, asset_class | 36 rows |
| `prices_inr.csv` | Daily prices **already in INR** for the 36 assets plus `^NSEI` and `^NDX` (USD assets converted with the daily USDINR series, per D20). Business-day calendar, 2012-01-02 to 2025-12-31, no NaNs | 3,653 x 38 |
| `usdinr.csv` | Synthetic daily USD/INR (starts near 51) | 3,653 rows |
| `regime_calendar.csv` | The regime windows and the drift / volatility parameters used to generate them | 7 rows |
| `presets.json` | `tech_heavy` (the demo persona Aman), `balanced_india`, `global_mix`, in the `/api/presets` contract shape | 3 presets |
| `dataset_full.csv` | The ML training table (D31 to D35): 18 features, raw forward targets, scores, labels, split | 4,680 rows |
| `eval.json` | Walk-forward results in the `/api/model/info` shape | |
| `demo_asset_stats.csv` | Per-asset stats and risk contribution for the demo portfolio over the last 3 years (contributions sum to 1) | 6 rows |
| `shock_2025_daily_log.csv` | Daily log for the demo portfolio from 2024-10-01 to 2025-07-04: value, drawdown, predicted label and probabilities, risk_score, realised forward label | 199 rows |
| `pipeline_log.txt` | The actual log of the generation and training run | |

## The 2025 shock (stylised)
- Window `shock_2025`: 2025-02-19 to 2025-04-08, followed by `rebound_2025` to 2025-06-30.
- Modelled on my general knowledge of the early-2025 tariff-driven selloff (US equities down roughly a fifth, Nasdaq worse, gold up). Your project docs do not define it, so treat the shape as an approximation.
- Realised in this file (local currency, window start to end): SPY -20.1%, QQQ -25.2%, NDX -23.4%, NSEI -7.7%, TLT -2.8%, GLD +3.5%.
- Demo portfolio (INR) fell from about 1.09M to 0.87M, with a worst drawdown of -27.0%.
- Other windows use your D52 dates: `covid_2020`, `bear_2022`, plus `bull_2021` and `recovery_2023`.

## `dataset_full.csv` columns
- `t`: feature date. Features use only the 252 trading days ending at `t`.
- 18 features: `vol_252, vol_63, vol_ratio, ann_return, max_dd, current_dd, sharpe, sortino, cvar95, avg_corr, diversification_ratio, hhi, top_weight, top_rc_share, beta_blend, equity_share, n_assets, bench_vol_63`.
- `fwd_vol`, `fwd_mdd`: realised over the next 126 trading days with weights held fixed. `fwd_end` is the last day of that window.
- `score = 0.5*fwd_vol/0.18 + 0.5*abs(fwd_mdd)/0.18`. `lookback_score` is the same formula on the last 126 days before `t` (for the persistence baseline).
- `label`, `lookback_label`: Low/Medium/High using cut-points from TRAIN rows only (33rd and 66th percentiles: 0.7305 and 0.9388).
- `split`: `train` (t < 2022-06-30, 3,540 rows), `purged` (210 rows), `test` (t >= 2023-01-01, 930 rows).
- `weights_json`: the portfolio, e.g. `{"NVDA": 0.31, "GLD": 0.12, ...}`.

## What the training run showed (synthetic, for understanding only)
Test set, 930 rows:

| Model | macro-F1 | accuracy | off-by-two |
|---|---|---|---|
| HGB + calibration | 0.462 | 0.502 | 0.111 |
| Logistic regression | 0.476 | 0.479 | 0.086 |
| Persistence | 0.446 | 0.451 | 0.103 |
| Majority class | 0.199 | 0.426 | 0.230 |

Median forward volatility by true class: Low 14.9%, Medium 18.5%, High 23.1%.

Read this honestly. The model beats persistence only slightly and does not beat logistic regression on macro-F1. That is the outcome D35 and the architecture doc already prepare you for: say so plainly and pitch calibration plus explainability. Real data may behave differently.

## Known quirks of this synthetic set
- The demo portfolio is predicted High on 196 of 199 days and its realised label is High every day, so this data will not show the "Make it Medium" flip as a model change. Use the optimizer's counterfactual for that.
- Single shared calendar. Real NSE and NASDAQ holidays differ (D22), so test your forward-fill logic on real data.
- NVDA's 3-year annualised return in `demo_asset_stats.csv` is about 0%, which is random-path noise, not a calibrated view.
